passages.context: The complete declaration was read: the occasion (the 19 July 1974 private letter to some episcopal conferences on the interpretation of canon 2335, since made public and given 'erroneous and tendentious interpretations'); the clarification 'without prejudice to the eventual norms of the new Code'; point 1 ('the present canonical discipline remains in full force and has not been modified in any way'); point 2 ('consequently, neither the excommunication nor the other penalties envisaged have been abrogated'); and point 3 (the 1974 letter was 'merely as a reminder of the general principles of interpretation of penal laws' for individual cases, not a permission for episcopal conferences 'to issue public pronouncements by way of a judgment of a general character on the nature of Masonic associations, which would imply a derogation from the aforesaid norms'). Signed Franjo Cardinal Seper, Prefect, and Fr. Jerome Hamer, O.P., Secretary, 17 February 1981.
passages.notes: Quoted wording extracted verbatim from the exact fetched response; the AAS printing was not consulted.

alternate_titles: Declaration Concerning Status of Catholics Becoming Freemasons
work.author: Sacred Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith
work.description: The CDF declaration of 17 February 1981 (AAS 73 [1981] 240-241), signed by Cardinal Seper, occasioned by the publication and misreading of the Congregation's private letter of 19 July 1974 on the interpretation of canon 2335 of the 1917 Code: it confirms that the canonical discipline remains in full force, that neither the excommunication nor the other penalties were abrogated, and that the 1974 letter did not authorize episcopal conferences to issue general judgments on the nature of Masonic associations derogating from those norms.
work.title: Declaration concerning the canonical discipline forbidding Catholics to enrol in Masonic associations (17 February 1981)
